title: Internal homogeneous functions and their normalized diagonal action
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on the coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with the sizes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $G$ be a profinite group. Use internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], their internal $G$-actions and section modules [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and the section-module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. For an equivariant internal module $J$ and $n\geq0$, define $\mathcal H_n(J)=\mathcal{H}om_A(A[\underline G^{n+1}],UJ)$ using the free module on the represented profinite power [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data] and the underived slice sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For $c\in\mathcal H_n(J)(S)$, $f:T\to S$, and a tuple $x_i:T\to G$, define its evaluation by applying the slice component $c_T$ to the canonical free generator $[x]$ of [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-generators]. A normalized homogeneous-function model consists of an equivariant module $H$, an identification of its underlying section-module sheaf with $\mathcal H_n(J)$, and the following action formula on every profinite base change $f:T\to S$: $\operatorname{ev}_f(g\cdot c)(x_i)=(g|_T)\cdot_J\operatorname{ev}_f(c)((g|_T)^{-1}x_i)$ for every $g\in C(S,G)$, section $c$ of $H$ over $S$, and tuple $x_i\in C(T,G)$. These data specify the meaning of the homogeneous action; this definition asserts neither existence nor injectivity.
